canonical_data: the working tree, saved session files and settings under the user's fx directory, workspace project configuration and AGENTS.md files, skill directories, and per-workspace MCP trust decisions
current_repo_note: Vercel's separate AI SDK harness adapter launches fx inside a Vercel sandbox over ACP; that adapter belongs to the AI SDK and is not part of this record.
strengths: A single static Zig binary with no runtime to install exposes file, shell with background process handles, web search and fetch, vision, skill, subagent, and MCP tools behind one policy check

Three permission modes, wildcard allow and deny rules per workspace or user, per-server trust prompts for project MCP configuration, and session-only grants give fine control, and subagents cannot exceed the parent's permissions

The same agent runs as an Agent Client Protocol server for editors, reads skills from other agents' directories and Claude-compatible MCP files, and ships as an npm SDK that runs natively or as WebAssembly
weaknesses: Released builds authenticate only through Vercel AI Gateway or ChatGPT and Grok subscriptions; the configurable local and OpenAI-compatible connections merged upstream on 2026-09-15 sit 61 commits past the latest tag, and their guide still tells readers to build from source
The default auto permission mode replaces human approval with a second model's review of the pending action, and that reviewer is a paid request that can hold or clear a call the user never sees
The README labels the project experimental, the first public release is from August 2026, and the changelog records breaking changes between 0.0.x releases
why_it_matters: A vendor-backed coding agent built to be embedded rather than to be a platform: one small native binary that speaks ACP, reads the skill and MCP conventions of other agents, and loads into a browser or server as a library.
